### FINDING 1 — NONFATAL — location: Remarks, third bullet ("Monotonicity cannot be dropped")
CLAIM AS WRITTEN: "an unbounded nondecreasing sequence does not merely fail to converge, it diverges to $+\infty$."
WHY IT FAILS: Not a failure — the sentence illustrates only the nondecreasing case of `lem-monotone-unbounded-diverges` and does not mention the dual nonincreasing case (diverges to $-\infty$, per that lemma's own second Remark). A reader closes this in well under 30 seconds by symmetry, and the omission asserts nothing false.
WHAT WOULD FIX IT: Optional only — could add "(dually for nonincreasing, to $-\infty$)"; not required.

### ASSESSMENT
I checked the current Statement, Facts & Assumptions, and Proof (steps 1.1–4.1) against the six declared dependencies and found every `[L#]` an exact, undistorted restatement of its target (monotone = nondecreasing-or-nonincreasing; the two-case monotone-convergence theorem; convergent-implies-bounded; the sequence/set boundedness definitions; the absolute-value equivalence). The proof's case split (nondecreasing / nonincreasing, `cases-exhaustive`) is licensed by L1 and closes both directions of the biconditional honestly; the title matches exactly what is proved.

I then focused on the repaired Remark, which replaced the sentence both judge lanes correctly flagged as fatal ("Without boundedness the forward direction is what fails" — false, since the forward direction is unconditional and the offered witness doesn't even converge, so it can't witness a failed implication). The replacement now states only true things: (a) the converse direction (bounded ⟹ converges) fails without monotonicity, correctly witnessed by `fs-bounded-implies-convergent` (an oscillating bounded sequence that provably does not converge — read in full, it matches); (b) the forward direction (converges ⟹ bounded) holds unconditionally for every sequence, matching both this item's own Statement and `lem-convergent-implies-bounded`'s Statement verbatim; (c) monotonicity sharpens rather than validates the forward direction's contrapositive for unbounded monotone sequences, and the cited sharpening — divergence to $+\infty$, strictly stronger than mere non-convergence — is exactly what `lem-monotone-unbounded-diverges` proves (read in full, its Statement and its own Remark confirming "$+\infty$ is not a limit... hence not convergent" both line up). The bold lead "Monotonicity cannot be dropped" is immediately and correctly qualified by the sentences that follow, so it does not overclaim once read in context. I also re-verified the two untouched Remarks (limit-naming via `thm-monotone-convergence`, and the Bolzano–Weierstrass usage via `thm-bolzano-weierstrass`, read in full) since a pre-existing defect anywhere in the item would still count; both are accurate.

I found no fatal defect in the current text.
